issues.legal_issue: A bill awaiting the President’s assent does not lapse when the State Legislative Assembly is dissolved.
material_facts: The Assembly passed the bill and the Governor reserved it for the President’s assent.
The Assembly was dissolved while the bill was awaiting that assent.
The President later returned the bill with a message, and a newly elected Assembly reconsidered and passed it.
issues.conclusion: The bill did not lapse on dissolution, and the President could validly consider it and give assent after its reconsideration.
issues.legal_principle: Article 196(5) exhaustively identifies the bills that lapse on dissolution and refers to bills pending in the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council, not bills pending assent. Article 196(3) also departs from the English rule by providing that prorogation does not cause pending bills to lapse. Articles 200 and 201 impose no time limit for the Governor or President to decide on a bill. Article 194(3), concerning legislative powers, privileges and immunities, does not import the English convention on dissolution into legislative procedure.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_enactment and bill_passed_by_assembly and bill_pending_for_head_of_state_assent and assembly_dissolved

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_enactment: A party in a constitutional challenge to an enactment disputes the validity of the enactment’s passage.
predicates.bill_passed_by_assembly: The legislature passed the bill before it was sent for assent.
predicates.bill_pending_for_head_of_state_assent: The bill was awaiting the head of state’s decision on assent when the legislature was dissolved.
predicates.assembly_dissolved: The legislative assembly was dissolved while the bill was awaiting assent.

issues.definition: When a bill has been passed and is awaiting the head of state’s assent at dissolution, the bill remains live despite the dissolution.

issues.legal_issue: A newly elected Legislative Assembly may reconsider a bill returned by the President under the constitutional reconsideration procedure.
material_facts: The President returned the bill with a message requesting reconsideration and suggesting amendments.
The Assembly that had originally passed the bill had been dissolved before the bill was returned.
A newly elected Assembly reconsidered the bill, adopted amendments, and passed it again.
issues.conclusion: Reconsideration by the newly elected Assembly did not violate the constitutional procedure for returned bills.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 200 and 201 do not require a returned bill to be reconsidered by the same Assembly that first passed it. The terms referring to return and reconsideration are satisfied when a successor Assembly considers the bill again; it may reject the bill or pass it again. Article 196 permits the bill to remain live through dissolution. Justice Ayyangar also agreed with the result on this procedural issue and relied on Attorney-General for New South Wales v. Pennie, [1896] A.C. 376, in treating the legislature as a continuing institution for this purpose.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_enactment and bill_returned_for_reconsideration and original_assembly_dissolved and successor_assembly_reconsiders_bill

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_enactment: A party in a constitutional challenge to an enactment disputes the validity of the enactment’s passage.
predicates.bill_returned_for_reconsideration: The head of state returned a bill with a message requesting that the legislature reconsider it.
predicates.original_assembly_dissolved: The assembly that first passed the bill was dissolved before reconsideration occurred.
predicates.successor_assembly_reconsiders_bill: A newly elected assembly considered the returned bill again.

issues.definition: When a bill is returned for reconsideration after the original assembly has been dissolved, a successor assembly may consider it again without invalidating the legislative process.

issues.legal_issue: Land held under a tenure that gives the holder proprietary rights in the soil and a direct obligation to pay land revenue to the State may be a local equivalent of an estate even without an intermediary.
material_facts: Approximately 900 acres were recorded as Pandaravaka Verumpattom lands.
The applicable proclamation provided that holders of those lands acquired full rights to the soil, subject to regularly paying State revenue.
The holder’s payment was assessed by reference to the land’s produce, but the proclamation treated it as State revenue rather than rent.
The majority found that the proclamation’s scheme established the holder’s proprietary interest in the land.
issues.conclusion: The Pandaravaka Verumpattom lands were a local equivalent of an estate under Article 31A(2)(a). Justice Ayyangar dissented on this classification, considering the tenure equivalent to ryotwari and therefore outside the definition of an estate.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 31A(2)(a), the meaning of estate includes the local equivalent of that expression under existing local land-tenure law. The majority identified the basic concept as land held by a proprietor of the soil who has a direct relationship with the State and pays land revenue; an intermediary is not essential. It relied on Shri Ram Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay, [1959] Supp. 1 S.C.R. 489; Atma Ram v. State of Punjab, [1959] Supp. 1 S.C.R. 748; Shri Mahadeo Paikaji Kolhe Yavatmal v. State of Bombay, [1962] 1 S.C.R. 733; and State of Bihar v. Rameshwar Pratap Narain Singh, [1962] 2 S.C.R. 382.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_agrarian_legislation and land_tenure_classification_disputed and local_law_grants_soil_proprietorship and holder_pays_state_land_revenue

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_agrarian_leg: A party challenges agrarian legislation on the ground that it interferes with constitutional rights.
predicates.land_tenure_classification_disputed: The parties dispute whether a category of landholding is an estate or its local equivalent.
predicates.local_law_grants_soil_proprietorship: The applicable local law gives the landholder proprietary rights in the soil.
predicates.holder_pays_state_land_revenue: The landholder is directly liable to pay land revenue to the State.

issues.definition: A disputed land tenure qualifies as an estate when local law gives its holder proprietary rights in the soil and the holder directly pays land revenue to the State, even if no intermediary exists.

issues.legal_issue: Land held under a tenure in which a landowner is recognised as proprietor and shares the produce with the cultivator and the State satisfies the definition of an estate.
material_facts: Approximately 350 acres were recorded as Puravaka lands.
Under the applicable proclamation, a Jenmi was recognised as proprietor of the land and entitled to share its produce with the cultivator and the State.
The petitioner held those lands under the Puravaka tenure.
issues.conclusion: The Puravaka lands constituted an estate under Article 31A(2)(a).
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(2)(a) includes an estate’s local equivalent under existing local land-tenure law and specifically includes janmam rights in Kerala. The majority held that the Puravaka tenure satisfied even the narrower conception advanced by the petitioner because the Jenmi was recognised as proprietor and shared the produce with the cultivator and the State. The majority’s construction of estate was supported by Shri Ram Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay, [1959] Supp. 1 S.C.R. 489; Atma Ram v. State of Punjab, [1959] Supp. 1 S.C.R. 748; Shri Mahadeo Paikaji Kolhe Yavatmal v. State of Bombay, [1962] 1 S.C.R. 733; and State of Bihar v. Rameshwar Pratap Narain Singh, [1962] 2 S.C.R. 382.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_agrarian_legislation and land_tenure_classification_disputed and local_law_recognizes_land_proprietor and produce_shared_with_cultivator_and_state

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_agrarian_leg: A party challenges agrarian legislation on the ground that it interferes with constitutional rights.
predicates.land_tenure_classification_disputed: The parties dispute whether a category of landholding is an estate or its local equivalent.
predicates.local_law_recognizes_land_proprietor: The applicable local law recognizes a landholder as proprietor of the land.
predicates.produce_shared_with_cultivator_and_state: The tenure provides for the land’s produce to be shared among the proprietor, the cultivator, and the State.

issues.definition: A disputed land tenure qualifies as an estate when local law recognizes a proprietor and provides for the produce to be shared with the cultivator and the State.

issues.legal_issue: Agrarian legislation operating on land that constitutes an estate is protected from challenge on the grounds that it violates the specified fundamental rights.
material_facts: The Act provided for acquisition of agricultural land exceeding statutory maximum extents.
The petitioner’s Pandaravaka Verumpattom and Puravaka lands were held to constitute estates under Article 31A(2)(a) by the majority.
The petitioner challenged the Act as inconsistent with fundamental rights.
issues.conclusion: The Act, insofar as it operated against the petitioner’s holdings, was protected by Article 31A(1)(a) and could not be challenged on the asserted grounds under Articles 14, 19, and 31; the petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(1)(a) protects a law providing for acquisition of an estate or rights in an estate from invalidation on the ground that it is inconsistent with or takes away or abridges the rights specified in that provision, provided the constitutional requirements for State legislation are met. Because the holdings were estates under Article 31A(2)(a), the majority did not decide the petitioner’s fundamental-rights challenge on its merits. Justice Ayyangar would have found the Pandaravaka lands outside the protection, but agreed that the Puravaka lands were covered.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_agrarian_leg: A party challenges agrarian legislation on the ground that it interferes with constitutional rights.
predicates.legislation_provides_for_acquisition_of_: The legislation provides for acquisition of land or rights in land.
predicates.affected_land_qualifies_as_estate: The land affected by the legislation qualifies as an estate or its local equivalent.
predicates.required_assent_obtained: The constitutionally required assent for the State legislation was obtained.

issues.definition: When agrarian legislation provides for acquisition of land that qualifies as an estate and the required assent is obtained, a challenge based on the specified fundamental rights is barred.
